neighbours.label: the last piece of a name right before a hyphen in a hyphenated proper name (Fearnley-, Bulwer-, Levallois-); predicts '-'
fire: We watched a cooking show hosted by Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall last night.
The novel was written by Edward Bulwer-Lytton in the nineteenth century.
Our hotel was in Stratford-upon-Avon, close to the theatre.
They spent the summer in Aix-en-Provence painting landscapes.
The actress Helena Bonham-Carter appeared at the premiere.
He finally bought a vintage Rolls-Royce at the auction.
Her office moved to Levallois-Perret, just outside Paris.
The state of Baden-Württemberg is home to many car makers.
quiet: We watched a cooking show hosted by Jamie Oliver last night.
The novel was written by Charles Dickens in the nineteenth century.
Our hotel was in Oxford, close to the theatre.
They spent the summer in Provence painting landscapes.
The actress Emma Thompson appeared at the premiere.
He finally bought a vintage Jaguar at the auction.
Her office moved to Versailles, just outside Paris.
The state of Bavaria is home to many car makers.

notes: Top examples are subword pieces (ley, is, wer) directly before '-' in double-barrelled names; the + pole's output suppresses '-' tokens, so this pole promotes the hyphen.
